verified_facts: collection is a topologically structured link-and-node representation of Great Britain's road, ferry, rail and path networks
rail network feature types were added in September 2023
collection updates are monthly and persistent identifiers with lifecycle information are supplied
Railway Link defines rail geometry and connectivity between two points
gauge, structure, physical level, railway use and track representation have distinct roles
the earliest consistent temporal snapshot date is 27 September 2023
Railway Node is a point that splits the railway network for connectivity
nodes occur at attribution changes, link intersections and link starts or ends
the earliest consistent temporal snapshot date is 27 September 2023
Railway Link Set depicts the full extent of a named railway as a continuous multiline feature
a cross-reference maps Railway Link Set identifiers and version dates to Railway Link identifiers
the same OSID may occur in more than one feature type
Railway Link includes train and tram tracks
rail geometry is generalised to preserve connectivity
Railway Link does not identify which Road Links carry tram tracks
Ferry Link represents public timetabled vehicular or pedestrian ferry connectivity
both terminals must be within Great Britain
start and end nodes are mandatory while route operator is nullable
Ferry Terminal is a logical connection between road or path and ferry networks
it references one Road Node or Path Node and one Ferry Node
it also references the related Site representation
Ferry Node is the point where Ferry Links start or end
one Ferry Node may serve multiple Ferry Links
every Ferry Node is referenced by at least one Ferry Link
RAMI integrates OS large-scale road data with National Street Gazetteer information
routing information includes hazards and vehicle restrictions
asset information includes maintenance responsibility and reinstatement conditions
Routing Structure covers barriers, bridges, tunnels, crossings and signals related to highways
the earliest consistent temporal snapshot date is 29 September 2022
RAMI groups rights and restrictions, advisory information and asset management separately
RAMI features reference the base road network rather than replacing it
Transport Link models road, path, rail or ferry connectivity between Transport Nodes
WayID is unique but not persistent
the earliest temporal snapshot date is 27 March 2024
documented known issues include null modal-change node types
some links present in OS NGD may be absent from the corresponding MRN release
known issues must be applied as fail-closed validation gates
OS APIs support OAuth2, key header and key query-parameter authentication
OAuth2 bearer tokens and API keys have different handling requirements
keys and tokens must be protected and rotated
token generation uses HTTP Basic authentication and client credentials
grant_type must be client_credentials
the response includes access_token, expires_in, issued_at and token_type
2xx indicates successful requests, 4xx request or access errors and 5xx service errors
304 permits cached conditional-GET reuse
429 and 503 require distinct retry handling
live projects are limited to 600 transactions per minute per API per project
development projects are limited to 50 transactions per minute per API per project
excess requests return HTTP 429 until the rate falls below the limit
the API exposes landing, conformance, collections, collection, schema, queryables, features and feature endpoints
CQL comparison, logical, array and INTERSECTS operators have explicit support
feature retrieval by OSID does not remove feature-type provenance
